newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka troops edge ahead amid rebel resistance.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka troops edge ahead amid rebel resistance.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops, slowed by fierce counter-attacks from separatist Tamil rebels, edged forward into northern rebel-held territory on Sunday, military officials in the north said.
Troops, who resumed their drive on Saturday after a five-day pause, had advanced about one km (half a mile) farther north of the former rebel-controlled town of Omanthai, they said.
"Troops are advancing today (Sunday) too. But we still don't have details of fresh fighting," a military spokesman in Colombo said.
Security sources in the north told Reuters the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) guerrillas were putting up stiff resistance and slowing the government advance.
Eleven soldiers, including one officer, were killed and more than 50 soldiers wounded in overnight fighting near the village of Rabakulam, just north of Omanthai, they said.
More than 100 rebels are believed to have been killed or wounded in the fighting, they added.
"The going was difficult. (Rebels) used the cover of bushes to fire rocket-propelled grenades at short range on to advancing tanks," a military official said.
A T-55 tank and an armoured troop carrier were destroyed by rebel fire while another tank was badly damaged, he said.
A statement by the LTTE's international secretariat in London said the rebels had lost only six fighters in fighting since Saturday.

Security forces captured Omanthai, 14 km (nine miles) north of the government-held town of Vavuniya, and Nedunkeni, 40 miles (25 km) northeast of Vavuniya, last week after a two-pronged thrust into the LTTE's northern Wanni heartland.

Some 20,000 troops launched "Operation Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory", from Vavuniya on May 13 in a bid to open a supply route to the Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north. Vavuniya lies 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.
Government forces rely on air and sea links to supply bases and civilians in Jaffna, the LTTE's former would-be homeland brought back under government control one year ago.
A Defence Ministry statement said 75 soldiers had died up to last Friday in the offensive, one of the military's biggest in the 13-year-old ethnic war. It said 126 soldiers were wounded.
Hospital sources, however, said some 600 soldiers had been wounded.

The rebel death toll up to Saturday was 65, according to the LTTE who are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in mainly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, but the LTTE say the toll is higher.
